title: Training Note — Hardship, Delinquency and Reinstatement Limits on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

# Training Note — Hardship, Delinquency and Reinstatement Limits on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

*Basis questions answered for finance desk agents. Every answer depends on the promotional term the Belrose Promotional Financing Plan was written on; the term-by-term figures are in the table at the foot of the note.*

**How long must a plan have been billing before a hardship arrangement may be enrolled?** For the stated minimum hardship tenure in whole months: 6 months on the 6-Month Deferred Interest Plan and the 12-Month Deferred Interest Plan, 9 months on the 18-Month Deferred Interest Plan and the 24-Month Equal Payment Plan, and 12 months on the 36-Month Equal Payment Plan and the 48-Month Bridal Equal Payment Plan.

**How many hardship arrangements may one plan ever be enrolled in?** 1 on each of the three deferred interest terms and 2 on each of the three equal payment terms, over the whole life of the plan.

**What share of the ordinary scheduled payment is billed during a reduced-payment arrangement?** 50 percent on the three deferred interest terms and 60 percent on the three equal payment terms.

**How long does a hardship arrangement run?** 3 whole months on the two shortest terms, 6 whole months on the 18-Month Deferred Interest Plan, the 24-Month Equal Payment Plan and the 36-Month Equal Payment Plan, and 12 whole months on the 48-Month Bridal Equal Payment Plan.

**For how many of those months does no interest accrue?** None on the two shortest terms, 3 months on the 18-Month Deferred Interest Plan and the 24-Month Equal Payment Plan, and 6 months on the two longest terms.

**At how many calendar days past due is a plan moved to the past due state?** 30 days on every term.

**At how many calendar days past due is a plan written off to collections?** 180 days on every term.

**From how many days past due may a plan still be brought current and reinstated?** Up to 60 days on the two shortest terms, up to 90 days on the 18-Month Deferred Interest Plan and the 24-Month Equal Payment Plan, and up to 120 days on the two longest terms.

## Figures by term

| Term | 6-Month Deferred Interest | 12-Month Deferred Interest | 18-Month Deferred Interest | 24-Month Equal Payment | 36-Month Equal Payment | 48-Month Bridal Equal Payment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole months billing before a hardship arrangement may be enrolled | 6 | 6 | 9 | 9 | 12 | 12 |
| Hardship arrangements one plan may ever be enrolled in | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Share of the ordinary scheduled payment billed during a reduced-payment arrangement | 50 percent | 50 percent | 50 percent | 60 percent | 60 percent | 60 percent |
| Length of a hardship arrangement, whole months | 3 | 3 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 12 |
| Whole months of the arrangement during which no interest accrues | 0 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 6 | 6 |
| Calendar days past due at which the plan is moved to past due | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Calendar days past due at which the plan is written off to collections | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 |
| Largest number of days past due from which a plan may still be reinstated | 60 | 60 | 90 | 90 | 120 | 120 |
